revision.comment: Marked this version for translation
revision.text: {{Navbar modding}} {{Page version|42.18.0}} {{Removed|text=As of {{ll|Build 42.13.0}}, this feature is deprecated to only depend on {{ll|translations}}.}} '''{{Code|DisplayName}}''' was used to set the display name of an item. This parameter was optional as of {{ll|Build 42.12.3}}. It was suggested to use item name {{ll|translations}} instead, which would take priority over this parameter. The priority order for the display name of an item was: # {{ll|Translations|Item name translation}} for current language # {{ll|Translations|Item name translation}} for English # {{Code|DisplayName}} parameter # Item full type Below is an example usage of the parameter: {{CodeSnip|code= DisplayName = Opened Canned Tomato, }} {{Note|type=warn|It is highly advised to use translations instead of this parameter, as it provides other modders the ability to translate your items into their own language with simple addons for your mod.}} == Using translation == {{Move|section=true|Item (scripts)|Item translation should now be explained in the main {{ll|Item (scripts)}} page since the DisplayName parameter is now deprecated as of {{ll|Build 42.13.0}}.}} Setup a {{ll|Translations#Commonly used files|translation file}} for one or more languages inside the folder {{Code|media/lua/shared/Translate/{language code}/}} with {{Code|{language code}} } listed in the {{ll|Translations#Languages|translations}} page. The file needs to be named {{Code|ItemName.json}} , which is case-insensitive: {{CodeSnip|code= media/ └── lua/ └── shared/ └── Translate/ ├── EN/ │ └── ItemName.json ├── FR/ │ └── ItemName.json └── ... }} Inside the file, add a key-value pair for each item you want to translate, using the full type of the item as the key and the desired display name as the value. Make sure to include commas after each line item. A single line item and last line items do not require a trailing comma. This will cause a parsing error. {{CodeSnip|code= { Base.CannedTomato = "Opened Canned Tomato", Base.CannedCorn = "Opened Canned Corn" } }} {{ll|Category:Item scripts parameters}}

revision.text: {{Navbar modding}} {{Page version|42.12.1}} {{Main|item (scripts)}} {{About|icons for {{ll|item (scripts)|item scripts}}|icons for {{ll|craftRecipe (scripts)|craftRecipe scripts}}|icon (craftRecipe)}} '''{{Code|icon}}''' specifies the Icon for an item, usually used in the inventory and crafting menus. The icon needs to be located inside the {{Code|media/textures/}} folder and must start with {{Code|Item_}} and be of the extension {{ll|File formats#Image formats|.png}}: {{CodeSnip|code = media/ └── textures/ └── Item_iconName.png }} Then reference the icon in the item script with: {{CodeSnip|code = Icon = iconName, }} To sum it up, follow these rules to set an icon for an item: * The icon file must be a PNG file (ending with {{Code|.png}} ). * The icon file must be located in the {{Code|media/textures/}} folder. * The icon file name must start with {{Code|Item_}} . * The icon file name must not include the {{Code|Item_}} prefix when referenced in the item script. * The icon file name must not include the {{Code|.png}} extension when referenced in the item script. {{Note|type=warn|A common mistake when an icon is not showing up is to forget the {{Code|Item_}} prefix.}} == Subfolders == Subfolders are not directly supported, but you can use some tricks to have one by doing: {{CodeSnip|code = Icon = subFolder/iconName, }} With the following file structure: {{CodeSnip|code = media/ └── textures/ └── Item_subFolder/ └── iconName.png }} == Food icons == Icons can be specified for rotten, cooked, and burned food by adding these suffix to the icon files: ; {{Code|Rotten}} or {{Code|Spoiled}} :Food that has rotten, meaning has passed the {{ll|DaysTotallyRotten}} value. ; {{Code|Cooked}} :Food that has been cooked, meaning has passed the {{ll|MinutesToCook}} value. ; {{Code|Overdone}} or {{Code|Burnt}} :Food that has been cooked to the point of burning, meaning has passed the {{ll|MinutesToBurn}} value. Food condition icons that do not exist will use the default icon value. === Example === Take a food item with the icon file defined as such: {{CodeSnip|code = Icon = iconName, }} To add variants based on food condition, you would have the following file structure: {{CodeSnip|code = media/ └── textures/ ├── Item_iconName.png ├── Item_iconNameCooked.png ├── Item_iconNameRotten.png └── Item_iconNameBurnt.png }} {{ll|Category:Item scripts parameters}}

{{Page version|41.78.19}}

<translate>
==== OnCooked ==== <!--T:1-->

<!--T:2-->
Specifies the name of the Lua function that is called when the item is cooked. The original item is passed as a parameter.
<syntaxhighlight lang="Java">
OnCooked = CannedFood_OnCooked,
</syntaxhighlight>

<!--T:3-->
<syntaxhighlight lang="Lua">
function CannedFood_OnCooked(cannedFood)
    local aged = cannedFood:getAge() / cannedFood:getOffAgeMax();
    cannedFood:setOffAgeMax(90);
    cannedFood:setOffAge(60);
    cannedFood:setAge(cannedFood:getOffAgeMax() * aged);
end
</syntaxhighlight>
</translate>

{{ll|Category:Item scripts parameters}}

revision.comment: Marked this version for translation
revision.text:
<languages />
{{Navbar modding}}
{{Page version|41.78.19}}

<translate>
==== OnCreate ==== <!--T:1-->

<!--T:2-->
Specifies a Lua function that will be called when the item spawns. An object is passed to the function as an argument. It is convenient to use to set the parameters of an object when it appears in the world.
<syntaxhighlight lang="Java">
OnCreate = Fishing.OnCreateFish,
</syntaxhighlight>

<!--T:3-->
<syntaxhighlight lang="Lua">
Fishing.OnCreateFish = function(_item)
    if not _item then return; end;
    local item = _item;
    local itemType = item:getFullType();
    local fish;
    for _, fishDef in ipairs(fishes) do
        if fishDef.item == itemType then
            fish = fishDef;
        end;
    end;
    if not fish then return; end;
    --
    local sizeName = "Small";
    local fishSizeNumber = ZombRand(100);
    if fishSizeNumber <= 20 then
        sizeName = "Big";
    elseif fishSizeNumber <= 30 then
        sizeName = "Medium";
    end;
    local baseWeightLb = item:getActualWeight();
    local size = nil;
    local weightKg = nil;

    <!--T:4-->
-- now we set the size (for the name) and weight (for hunger) according to his size (little, medium and big)
    if sizeName == "Small" then
        size = ZombRand(fish.little.minSize, fish.little.maxSize);
        weightKg = size / fish.little.weightChange;
    elseif sizeName == "Medium" then
        size = ZombRand(fish.medium.minSize, fish.medium.maxSize);
        weightKg = size / fish.medium.weightChange;
    else
        size = ZombRand(fish.big.minSize, fish.big.maxSize);
        weightKg = size / fish.big.weightChange;
    end

    <!--T:5-->
local nutritionFactor = 2.2 * weightKg / baseWeightLb;
    item:setCalories(item:getCalories() * nutritionFactor);
    item:setLipids(item:getLipids() * nutritionFactor);
    item:setCarbohydrates(item:getCarbohydrates() * nutritionFactor);
    item:setProteins(item:getProteins() * nutritionFactor);
    local wScale = fish.scaleCoeff[math.floor(size / 10.0)]
    if wScale == nil then wScale = 1.0 end
    item:setWorldScale(wScale);

    <!--T:6-->
-- hunger reduction is weight of the fish div by 6, and set it to negative
    item:setBaseHunger(- weightKg / 6);
    item:setHungChange(item:getBaseHunger());
    -- weight is kg * 2.2 (in pound)
    item:setActualWeight(weightKg * 2.2);
    item:setCustomWeight(true);
end
</syntaxhighlight>
</translate>

{{ll|Category:Item scripts parameters}}

{{Page version|42.13.0}}
{{About|the parameter used in {{ll|Item (scripts)|item scripts}} to assign tags to items.|a list of tags in the base game|Item tag}}
{{Stub|As of {{ll|Build 42.13.0}}, the '''ItemTags''' parameter has been reshaped to use an enum system instead of string values. This page is a stub and needs to be expanded to document this new system which depends on {{ll|registries}}.}}
<translate>
<!--T:1-->
'''ItemTag'''s serve as labels that can be assigned to multiple items to identify recurring characteristics or functionalities, for example knives, bottles etc. They can notably be used in {{ll|CraftRecipe}}s to define required items by their tags instead of specific item names.

== See also == <!--T:2-->

<!--T:3-->
* {{ll|Item tag}} - a list of tags in the base game.
</translate>

{{ll|Category:Item scripts parameters}}

revision.comment: Marked this version for translation
revision.text: {{Navbar modding}} {{Page version|42.13.1}} The '''{{Code|ItemType}}''' parameter defines the class the item will be instantiated as. Every items are created as an {{JavaObject|InventoryItem|package=zombie/inventory|customDoc=https://demiurgequantified.github.io/ProjectZomboidJavaDocs/}} 's subclass, based on the value of this parameter. The various parameters the {{ll|item (scripts)|item script}} can have are dependent on the class of the item; such as food items will hold nutritional values and weapon items will hold damage values. The possible values are: * base:alarmclock * base:alarmclockclothing * base:animal * base:clothing * base:container * base:drainable * base:food * base:key * base:literature * base:map * base:moveable * base:normal * base:radio * base:weapon * base:weaponpart Below is an example for the parameter: {{CodeSnip| code = ItemType = base:food, }} {{Note|In {{ll|Build 42.12.0}} patch note, it was announced that work is being put on replacing the {{Code|Type}} system by the ECS system that {{ll|Fluid (scripts)}} notably use, which should make items way more flexible in their definitions, so you could add a radio ECS to an item for it be a radio, or food ECS etc. {{Quote|text=In the future, it'll help us in making ECS items work - so items will have components, instead of having a "Food.class" item, we'll have a simple InventoryItem and add a component "Nutrition" to it. The intent is for it to ultimately simplify our code a lot.|author=[https://theindiestone.com/forums/index.php?/topic/86939-build-42120-unstable-released/ The Indie Stone]}} }} {{ll|Category:Item scripts parameters}}

==== AcceptItemFunction ====

Specifies the name of a Lua function that is called to check if the given item can be placed in the container. The original item is passed as a parameter, a Boolean parameter (true or false) is returned.
<syntaxhighlight lang="Java">
AcceptItemFunction = AcceptItemFuncForFannyPack,
</syntaxhighlight>
<syntaxhighlight lang="Java">
function AcceptItemFuncForFannyPack(item)
    return item:getActualWeight() < 0.5;
end
</syntaxhighlight>

{{ll|Category:Item scripts parameters}}

revision.text:
<languages />
{{Navbar modding}}
{{Page version|41.78.19}}

<translate>
==== OnEat ==== <!--T:1-->

<!--T:2-->
Specifies a Lua function to be called when an item is eaten. Food, character and percent of food eaten is passed as parameters.
<syntaxhighlight lang="Java">
OnEat = OnEat_Cigarettes,
</syntaxhighlight>

<!--T:3-->
<syntaxhighlight lang="Lua">
function OnEat_Cigarettes(food, character, percent)
    local script = food:getScriptItem()
    percent = percent * (food:getStressChange() * 100) / script:getStressChange()
    local bodyDamage = character:getBodyDamage()
    local stats = character:getStats()
    if character:HasTrait("Smoker") then
        bodyDamage:setUnhappynessLevel(bodyDamage:getUnhappynessLevel() - 10 * percent);
        if bodyDamage:getUnhappynessLevel() < 0 then
            bodyDamage:setUnhappynessLevel(0);
        end
        stats:setStress(stats:getStress() - 10 * percent);
        if stats:getStress() < 0 then
            stats:setStress(0);
        end
        local reduceSFC = stats:getMaxStressFromCigarettes()
        stats:setStressFromCigarettes(stats:getStressFromCigarettes() - reduceSFC * percent);
        character:setTimeSinceLastSmoke(stats:getStressFromCigarettes() / stats:getMaxStressFromCigarettes());
    else
        bodyDamage:setFoodSicknessLevel(bodyDamage:getFoodSicknessLevel() + 14 * percent);
        if bodyDamage:getFoodSicknessLevel() > 100 then
            bodyDamage:setFoodSicknessLevel(100);
        end
    end
end
</syntaxhighlight>
</translate>

{{ll|Category:Item scripts parameters}}

{{Navbar modding}}
{{Page version|41.78.19}}

==== ColorRed ====

Sets the red color parameter (0-255) to use in the tint of the item's icon and to determine the color of the light bulb's glow.
<syntaxhighlight lang="Java">
ColorRed = 228,
</syntaxhighlight>

{{ll|Category:Item scripts parameters}}

{{Navbar modding}}
{{Page version|41.78.19}}

==== CantBeFrozen ====

If the parameter is true, then the item cannot be frozen in the refrigerator.
<syntaxhighlight lang="Java">
CantBeFrozen = true,
</syntaxhighlight>

{{ll|Category:Item scripts parameters}}

{{About|item parameter|player parameter|Nutrition#Nutrients}}

==== Carbohydrates ====

Specifies the number of carbohydrates in the item.
<syntaxhighlight lang="Java">
Carbohydrates = 28,
</syntaxhighlight>

{{ll|Category:Item scripts parameters}}

revision.comment: Updating to match new version of source page
revision.text:
<languages />
{{Navbar modding}}
{{Page version|41.78.19}}

==== CombatSpeedModifier ====

Used for clothes. Affects weapon attack speed.
<syntaxhighlight lang="Java">
CombatSpeedModifier = 0.9,
</syntaxhighlight>

{{ll|Category:Item scripts parameters}}

revision.comment: Updating to match new version of source page
revision.text:
<languages />
{{Navbar modding}}
{{Page version|41.78.19}}

==== ShellFallSound ====

Sets the sound of the dropped shell.
<syntaxhighlight lang="Java">
ShellFallSound = M9CartridgeFall,
</syntaxhighlight>

{{ll|Category:Item scripts parameters}}

revision.comment: Updating to match new version of source page
revision.text:
<languages />
{{Navbar modding}}
{{Page version|41.78.19}}

==== EatType ====

Sets the animation variable that will be used when the item is eaten (FoodType Variable in .xml files).
<syntaxhighlight lang="Java">
EatType = Kettle,
</syntaxhighlight>

{{ll|Category:Item scripts parameters}}

revision.comment: Updating to match new version of source page
revision.text:
<languages />
{{Navbar modding}}
{{Page version|41.78.19}}

==== ConditionAffectsCapacity ====

If the parameter is true, then the state of the item will affect the capacity of the item.
<syntaxhighlight lang="Java">
ConditionAffectsCapacity = true,
</syntaxhighlight>

{{ll|Category:Item scripts parameters}}

revision.comment: Updating to match new version of source page
revision.text:
<languages />
{{Navbar modding}}
{{Page version|41.78.19}}

==== CanBeReused ====

Determines if the trap can be picked up and used again. Does not work with sensory traps.
<syntaxhighlight lang="Java">
CanBeReused = true,
</syntaxhighlight>

{{ll|Category:Item scripts parameters}}

revision.comment: Updating to match new version of source page
revision.text:
<languages />
{{Navbar modding}}
{{Page version|41.78.19}}

==== WetCooldown ====

Cooldown wetness modifier for item.
<syntaxhighlight lang="Java">
WetCooldown = 8000,
</syntaxhighlight>

{{ll|Category:Item scripts parameters}}

revision.comment: Updating to match new version of source page
revision.text:
<languages />
{{Navbar modding}}
{{Page version|41.78.19}}

==== Count ====

Determines how many items of this type will appear when spawning/crafting this type of item.
<syntaxhighlight lang="Java">
Count = 5,
</syntaxhighlight>

{{ll|Category:Item scripts parameters}}

revision.comment: Updating to match new version of source page
revision.text:
<languages />
{{Navbar modding}}
{{Page version|41.78.19}}

==== DamageModifier ====

Sets the damage modifier for the WeaponPart.
<syntaxhighlight lang="Java">
DamageModifier = 0.5,
</syntaxhighlight>

{{ll|Category:Item scripts parameters}}

revision.comment: Updating to match new version of source page
revision.text:
<languages />
{{Navbar modding}}
{{Page version|41.78.19}}

==== UseSelf ====

Used for weapons. If the parameter is true, then the weapon will be spent on use.
<syntaxhighlight lang="Java">
UseSelf = true,
</syntaxhighlight>

{{ll|Category:Item scripts parameters}}

revision.comment: Updating to match new version of source page
revision.text:
<languages />
{{Navbar modding}}
{{Page version|41.78.19}}

==== CanBeWrite ====

Determines whether it is possible to write in the given item.
<syntaxhighlight lang="Java">
CanBeWrite = true,
</syntaxhighlight>

{{ll|Category:Item scripts parameters}}

revision.comment: Updating to match new version of source page
revision.text:
<languages />
{{Navbar modding}}
{{Page version|41.78.19}}

==== ColorBlue ====

Sets the blue color parameter (0-255) to use in the tint of the item's icon and to determine the color of the light bulb's glow.
<syntaxhighlight lang="Java">
ColorBlue = 0,
</syntaxhighlight>

{{ll|Category:Item scripts parameters}}

revision.comment: Updating to match new version of source page
revision.text:
<languages />
{{Navbar modding}}
{{Page version|41.78.19}}

==== PoisonDetectionLevel ====

The parameter indicates at what level of cooking it will be clear that this food item is poisonous. The formula for calculating the level of cooking skill that will determine if food is poisonous: '''CookingSkillLevel >= 10 - PoisonDetectionLevel'''
<syntaxhighlight lang="Java">
PoisonDetectionLevel = 7,
</syntaxhighlight>

{{ll|Category:Item scripts parameters}}

revision.comment: Updating to match new version of source page
revision.text:
<languages />
{{Navbar modding}}
{{Page version|41.78.19}}

==== ReloadTimeModifier ====

Reload time modifier (WeaponPart item). Negative number to speed up reload time.
<syntaxhighlight lang="Java">
ReloadTimeModifier = -5,
</syntaxhighlight>

{{ll|Category:Item scripts parameters}}

revision.comment: Updating to match new version of source page
revision.text:
<languages />
{{Navbar modding}}
{{Page version|41.78.19}}

==== DangerousUncooked ====

Used for food. If the parameter is true, then there is a chance to get an infection (Just an infection, not a zombie virus).
<syntaxhighlight lang="Java">
DangerousUncooked = true,
</syntaxhighlight>

{{ll|Category:Item scripts parameters}}

revision.comment: Updating to match new version of source page
revision.text:
<languages />
{{Navbar modding}}
{{Page version|41.78.19}}

==== DoorDamage ====

Parameter for weapons. A modifier that affects how much damage is dealt to a door/vehicle with a given weapon.
<syntaxhighlight lang="Java">
DoorDamage = 9,
</syntaxhighlight>

{{ll|Category:Item scripts parameters}}

revision.comment: Updating to match new version of source page
revision.text:
<languages />
{{Navbar modding}}
{{Page version|41.78.19}}

==== DamageMakeHole ====

Parameter for weapons. Determines if the weapon will inflict damage to clothing, which will leave a hole.
<syntaxhighlight lang="Java">
DamageMakeHole = true,
</syntaxhighlight>

{{ll|Category:Item scripts parameters}}

revision.comment: Updating to match new version of source page
revision.text:
<languages />
{{Navbar modding}}
{{Page version|41.78.19}}

==== EvolvedRecipe ====

Indicates in which Evolved recipes this item can participate as an ingredient. And how much the item will be spent per use. The Cooked parameter determines whether the dish should be cooked before adding the ingredient.
<syntaxhighlight lang="Java">
EvolvedRecipe = Soup:3;Stew:3;Stir fry:3;Burger:3|Cooked;Salad:3;Sandwich:3,
</syntaxhighlight>

{{ll|Category:Item scripts parameters}}

revision.comment: Updating to match new version of source page
revision.text:
<languages />
{{Navbar modding}}
{{Page version|41.78.19}}

==== CloseSound ====

Specifies the sound that will be played when the item (InventoryContainer) is closed.
<syntaxhighlight lang="Java">
CloseSound = CloseBag,
</syntaxhighlight>

{{ll|Category:Item scripts parameters}}

revision.text: {{Navbar modding}} {{Page version|42.13.1}} The '''{{Code|ItemType}}''' parameter defines the class the item will be instantiated as. Every items are created as an {{JavaObject|InventoryItem|package=zombie/inventory|customDoc=https://demiurgequantified.github.io/ProjectZomboidJavaDocs/}}'s subclass, based on the value of this parameter. The various parameters the {{ll|item (scripts)|item script}} can have are dependent on the class of the item; such as food items will hold nutritional values and weapon items will hold damage values. The possible values are: * base:alarmclock * base:alarmclockclothing * base:animal * base:clothing * base:container * base:drainable * base:food * base:key * base:literature * base:map * base:moveable * base:normal * base:radio * base:weapon * base:weaponpart Below is an example for the parameter: {{CodeSnip| code = ItemType = base:food, }} {{Note|In {{ll|Build 42.12.0}} patch note, it was announced that work is being put on replacing the {{Code|Type}} system by the ECS system that {{ll|Fluid (scripts)}} notably use, which should make items way more flexible in their definitions, so you could add a radio ECS to an item for it be a radio, or food ECS etc. {{Quote|text=In the future, it'll help us in making ECS items work - so items will have components, instead of having a "Food.class" item, we'll have a simple InventoryItem and add a component "Nutrition" to it. The intent is for it to ultimately simplify our code a lot.|author=[https://theindiestone.com/forums/index.php?/topic/86939-build-42120-unstable-released/ The Indie Stone]}} }} {{ll|Category:Item scripts parameters}}

revision.comment: Updating to match new version of source page
revision.text: {{Navbar modding}} {{Page version|42.12.1}} {{Main|item (scripts)}} {{About|icons for {{ll|item (scripts)|item scripts}}|icons for {{ll|craftRecipe (scripts)|craftRecipe scripts}}|icon (craftRecipe)}} '''{{Code|icon}}''' specifies the Icon for an item, usually used in the inventory and crafting menus. The icon needs to be located inside the {{Code|media/textures/}} folder and must start with {{Code|Item_}} and be of the extension {{ll|File formats#Image formats|.png}}: {{CodeSnip|code = media/ └── textures/ └── Item_iconName.png }} Then reference the icon in the item script with: {{CodeSnip|code = Icon = iconName, }} To sum it up, follow these rules to set an icon for an item: * The icon file must be a PNG file (ending with {{Code|.png}}). * The icon file must be located in the {{Code|media/textures/}} folder. * The icon file name must start with {{Code|Item_}}. * The icon file name must not include the {{Code|Item_}} prefix when referenced in the item script. * The icon file name must not include the {{Code|.png}} extension when referenced in the item script. {{Note|type=warn|A common mistake when an icon is not showing up is to forget the {{Code|Item_}} prefix.}} == Subfolders == Subfolders are not directly supported, but you can use some tricks to have one by doing: {{CodeSnip|code = Icon = subFolder/iconName, }} With the following file structure: {{CodeSnip|code = media/ └── textures/ └── Item_subFolder/ └── iconName.png }} == Food icons == Icons can be specified for rotten, cooked, and burned food by adding these suffix to the icon files: ;{{Code|Rotten}} or {{Code|Spoiled}} :Food that has rotten, meaning has passed the {{ll|DaysTotallyRotten}} value. ;{{Code|Cooked}} :Food that has been cooked, meaning has passed the {{ll|MinutesToCook}} value. ;{{Code|Overdone}} or {{Code|Burnt}} :Food that has been cooked to the point of burning, meaning has passed the {{ll|MinutesToBurn}} value. Food condition icons that do not exist will use the default icon value. === Example === Take a food item with the icon file defined as such: {{CodeSnip|code = Icon = iconName, }} To add variants based on food condition, you would have the following file structure: {{CodeSnip|code = media/ └── textures/ ├── Item_iconName.png ├── Item_iconNameCooked.png ├── Item_iconNameRotten.png └── Item_iconNameBurnt.png }} {{ll|Category:Item scripts parameters}}

==== OnCreate ====

Specifies a Lua function that will be called when the item spawns. An object is passed to the function as an argument. It is convenient to use to set the parameters of an object when it appears in the world.
<syntaxhighlight lang="Java">
OnCreate = Fishing.OnCreateFish,
</syntaxhighlight>

<syntaxhighlight lang="Lua">
Fishing.OnCreateFish = function(_item)
    if not _item then return; end;
    local item = _item;
    local itemType = item:getFullType();
    local fish;
    for _, fishDef in ipairs(fishes) do
        if fishDef.item == itemType then
            fish = fishDef;
        end;
    end;
    if not fish then return; end;
    --
    local sizeName = "Small";
    local fishSizeNumber = ZombRand(100);
    if fishSizeNumber <= 20 then
        sizeName = "Big";
    elseif fishSizeNumber <= 30 then
        sizeName = "Medium";
    end;
    local baseWeightLb = item:getActualWeight();
    local size = nil;
    local weightKg = nil;

    -- now we set the size (for the name) and weight (for hunger) according to his size (little, medium and big)
    if sizeName == "Small" then
        size = ZombRand(fish.little.minSize, fish.little.maxSize);
        weightKg = size / fish.little.weightChange;
    elseif sizeName == "Medium" then
        size = ZombRand(fish.medium.minSize, fish.medium.maxSize);
        weightKg = size / fish.medium.weightChange;
    else
        size = ZombRand(fish.big.minSize, fish.big.maxSize);
        weightKg = size / fish.big.weightChange;
    end

    local nutritionFactor = 2.2 * weightKg / baseWeightLb;
    item:setCalories(item:getCalories() * nutritionFactor);
    item:setLipids(item:getLipids() * nutritionFactor);
    item:setCarbohydrates(item:getCarbohydrates() * nutritionFactor);
    item:setProteins(item:getProteins() * nutritionFactor);
    local wScale = fish.scaleCoeff[math.floor(size / 10.0)]
    if wScale == nil then wScale = 1.0 end
    item:setWorldScale(wScale);

    -- hunger reduction is weight of the fish div by 6, and set it to negative
    item:setBaseHunger(- weightKg / 6);
    item:setHungChange(item:getBaseHunger());
    -- weight is kg * 2.2 (in pound)
    item:setActualWeight(weightKg * 2.2);
    item:setCustomWeight(true);
end
</syntaxhighlight>

{{ll|Category:Item scripts parameters}}

revision.comment: Updating to match new version of source page
revision.text:
<languages />
{{Navbar modding}}
{{Page version|41.78.19}}

==== OnEat ====

Specifies a Lua function to be called when an item is eaten. Food, character and percent of food eaten is passed as parameters.
<syntaxhighlight lang="Java">
OnEat = OnEat_Cigarettes,
</syntaxhighlight>

<syntaxhighlight lang="Lua">
function OnEat_Cigarettes(food, character, percent)
    local script = food:getScriptItem()
    percent = percent * (food:getStressChange() * 100) / script:getStressChange()
    local bodyDamage = character:getBodyDamage()
    local stats = character:getStats()
    if character:HasTrait("Smoker") then
        bodyDamage:setUnhappynessLevel(bodyDamage:getUnhappynessLevel() - 10 * percent);
        if bodyDamage:getUnhappynessLevel() < 0 then
            bodyDamage:setUnhappynessLevel(0);
        end
        stats:setStress(stats:getStress() - 10 * percent);
        if stats:getStress() < 0 then
            stats:setStress(0);
        end
        local reduceSFC = stats:getMaxStressFromCigarettes()
        stats:setStressFromCigarettes(stats:getStressFromCigarettes() - reduceSFC * percent);
        character:setTimeSinceLastSmoke(stats:getStressFromCigarettes() / stats:getMaxStressFromCigarettes());
    else
        bodyDamage:setFoodSicknessLevel(bodyDamage:getFoodSicknessLevel() + 14 * percent);
        if bodyDamage:getFoodSicknessLevel() > 100 then
            bodyDamage:setFoodSicknessLevel(100);
        end
    end
end
</syntaxhighlight>

</syntaxhighlight>

<syntaxhighlight lang="Lua">
function CannedFood_OnCooked(cannedFood)
    local aged = cannedFood:getAge() / cannedFood:getOffAgeMax();
    cannedFood:setOffAgeMax(90);
    cannedFood:setOffAge(60);
    cannedFood:setAge(cannedFood:getOffAgeMax() * aged);
end
</syntaxhighlight>

revision.text: {{Navbar modding}} {{Page version|42.18.0}} {{Removed|text=As of {{ll|Build 42.13.0}}, this feature is deprecated to only depend on {{ll|translations}}.}} '''{{Code|DisplayName}}''' was used to set the display name of an item. This parameter was optional as of {{ll|Build 42.12.3}}. It was suggested to use item name {{ll|translations}} instead, which would take priority over this parameter. The priority order for the display name of an item was: # {{ll|Translations|Item name translation}} for current language # {{ll|Translations|Item name translation}} for English # {{Code|DisplayName}} parameter # Item full type Below is an example usage of the parameter: {{CodeSnip|code= DisplayName = Opened Canned Tomato, }} {{Note|type=warn|It is highly advised to use translations instead of this parameter, as it provides other modders the ability to translate your items into their own language with simple addons for your mod.}} == Using translation == {{Move|section=true|Item (scripts)|Item translation should now be explained in the main {{ll|Item (scripts)}} page since the DisplayName parameter is now deprecated as of {{ll|Build 42.13.0}}.}} Setup a {{ll|Translations#Commonly used files|translation file}} for one or more languages inside the folder {{Code|media/lua/shared/Translate/{language code}/}} with {{Code|{language code}}} listed in the {{ll|Translations#Languages|translations}} page. The file needs to be named {{Code|ItemName.json}}, which is case-insensitive: {{CodeSnip|code= media/ └── lua/ └── shared/ └── Translate/ ├── EN/ │ └── ItemName.json ├── FR/ │ └── ItemName.json └── ... }} Inside the file, add a key-value pair for each item you want to translate, using the full type of the item as the key and the desired display name as the value. Make sure to include commas after each line item. A single line item and last line items do not require a trailing comma. This will cause a parsing error. {{CodeSnip|code= { Base.CannedTomato = "Opened Canned Tomato", Base.CannedCorn = "Opened Canned Corn" } }} {{ll|Category:Item scripts parameters}}

{{Stub|As of {{ll|Build 42.13.0}}, the '''ItemTags''' parameter has been reshaped to use an enum system instead of string values. This page is a stub and needs to be expanded to document this new system which depends on {{ll|registries}}.}}
'''ItemTag'''s serve as labels that can be assigned to multiple items to identify recurring characteristics or functionalities, for example knives, bottles etc. They can notably be used in {{ll|CraftRecipe}}s to define required items by their tags instead of specific item names.

== See also ==

* {{ll|Item tag}} - a list of tags in the base game.
